To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) AC losses of the HTS DC cable depend on the frequency of ripple current and current imbalance; 2) The AC loss increases with increasing frequency and imbalance of current.

the frequency characteristics of current ripple in the DC HTS cable are determined by the current imbalance and the cable length, and the AC losses depend on the frequency of the ripple and the current imbalance in the HTS cable.
the current imbalance is an important factor that affects the efficiency of HTs cables.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the AC losses in the DC HTS cable and the influence of current imbalance on these losses.
the development of methods of reducing current imbalance, AC losses and, consequently, the increase of the efficiency of HTs cable systems.
the development of the theory for the current imbalance and AC losses in long distance DC HTC cables.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AC losses of DC HTS cables are determined by current imbalance, and the latter depends on the resistance of the soldered joints of superconducting tapes.
the current imbalance and ripple currents are the most significant factors for the efficiency of the HTS cable systems.
the DC HTS cable system is the most promising for long distance transmission lines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current imbalance and AC losses are the two most serious problems of DC HTS cables.
the current imbalance in the DC cable leads to the appearance of AC component of the current and, consequently, to the increase in AC losses.
the AC losses of DC cables with current imbalance is much lower than the AC losses of AC cables.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current imbalance is the main factor of the AC losses in DC HTS cables.
the AC losses in HTS DC cables with current imbalance are significantly higher than in the case of the balanced current.
the AC losses are not negligible and should be taken into account in the design of DC HTS cables.
